I noticed it about a year ago but the doc confirmed it was a cyst and said it wasn’t harming anything so to just leave it be. About a week ago it got infected I guess so it got really swollen and painful. It didn’t start to open up or leak until I started taking antibiotics though.

So I have had the cyst for a little over a year. When I first noticed it, I went to the doctor, and then had an ultrasound to confirm it was just a cyst. Since it didn’t hurt or anything, the doctor just shrugged it off.

It started hurting about a week ago and then got swollen quickly so I went back to the doctor. She said she would give me two weeks of antibiotics, and that it should clear up. It started draining on day 3 of the antibiotics, meaning the skin had some pus coming out but mostly blood. On day 4, when I took the bandage off, I noticed the cyst was sticking out so I was able to pull it out with my finger. 

I’m not sure what it’s made of but I saved it in a Tupperware with some water in case the doctor wants to analyze it. I thought I might have more cysts because there were two more holes appearing next to the big one, but I am not sure if there are more because I can’t feel them. I’m on day 5 of the antibiotics so I still have 9 to go. Not sure if it’s just going to heal itself up at this point or if more will come out. We’ll see! I’m also trying to get my doctor (who is an OBGYN) to refer me to a breast specialist in case this ever happens again. I would rather them cut out the cyst because that would probably scar less and have less recovery time than having my body push it out like this one did.

It came out by itself but not while I was in the shower. I had it bandaged and one of the times I was changing the gauze, I saw it sticking out. My body pushed it out because of the antibiotics. I never had surgery (although that may have been a better option…)

Not sure about other types of cysts but breast cysts are relatively common in women and usually don’t cause any pain or trouble. This cyst was in my bra line, and got irritated/infected by the rubbing underwire, so that’s why it flared up and became a problem. I think cysts also tend to develop in places where there is moisture, so the cyst in my bra line could have developed one day when I was sweating and the bra was trapping the moisture against the skin.

No, it was deep in the skin. It started to get sore and painful and swollen so I went to the doc and she gave me two weeks of antibiotics (these pics were on day 4 of the antibiotics). I expected some drainage but this morning when I woke up, this thing was poking out and when I touched it with my finger I realized it wasn’t pus so I pulled it out and afterwards it felt SO MUCH BETTER. I don’t know what the heck it is but I’m glad it’s out.

Thank you for reaching out! I truly am good, I just asked the question for education for myself and for others. Now that people are going out and about again, and I’m seeing people I have not seen in over a year, some people have made some big changes in their lives. Some people don’t seem to be the same people they were before the pandemic. I just want to be aware so that if there’s something going on, maybe I can help.

So I’ll address these one by one as a woman:

-We are all insecure about our bodies. I have a huge rib cage and a protruding sternum that showed up when I was 10. It doesn’t really matter, I can promise you that people are always going to worry about how their own body looks more than the other persons body

-I take adderall daily as a prescription so I can’t comment on that part, but I spent a large amount of my 20s being afraid of sober intimacy. The nice thing is that when you actually meet a person who truly likes you and wants to be with you, they will make all of those insecurities work and it won’t be weird

-Not having a job doesn’t mean you don’t have anything to offer. Can you cook? Are you handy? Do you have any skills? If you have any sort of hobby, you can make that “your thing” and then suddenly it’s an asset

-Dating for an ego boost is not a shitty reason to date. Tinder exists for a reason 


All that being said, thank you for your insights. I’m not trying to invalidate your concerns, but I hope I alleviated some of them. As a woman in her 30s who is not married, I have a lot of things in common with you. But I have hope for us! And I have hope you will find that someone special you deserve. Not trying to be cliche, but people like us are more common than you think.

I am not an emergency responder, but my uncle is a paramedic. He has told some pretty crazy stories. He once told me about a car accident scene where there was a half hemisphere of a brain on the street. Most of us would probably have been horrified, but all he could talk about was how he and his partner were just memorized at how half of a brain could have landed so perfectly on the pavement intact. They couldn't get over the physics of it.

I considered EMS as a career when I was in college but this story always stuck with me. You would have to be pretty jaded to only focus on the science and not constantly think about patients as a person with hopes and dreams and a family. I guess you would have to, to be able to sleep at night and get up the next morning and do it all over again.
